title: S6003 (NSIC Rc 376H) Hybrid Rice: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: S6003 (NSIC Rc 376H): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: S6003 is NSIC Rc 376H, a hybrid rice for irrigated lowland: about 111 days and 6.3 tonnes per hectare on average. See its ratings.
excerpt: NSIC Rc 376H is a hybrid rice variety for irrigated lowland, sold as S6003 or Frontline S6003 and known locally as Mestiso 59. The NSIC approved it in 2014. Syngenta bred it. It matures in about 111 days and averages 6.3 tonnes per hectare, with a top yield of 10.4 tonnes in trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for S6003 or Frontline S6003, or rice variety 376H, this is the one. Compare it with the other varieties in our [rice variety finder](/rice-varieties) before you buy seed. Also read our guide to [rice varieties in the Philippines](/crops/rice-varieties-philippines) for how inbreds, hybrids and special rice differ.

**Watch out for:** rice blast, bacterial leaf blight, tungro, brown planthopper, green leafhopper, sheath blight.

blocks.text: How much does NSIC Rc 376H yield?

On average it gives 6.3 tonnes per hectare. That is about 126 cavans of 50 kilograms of palay. It sits below the average of the 180 irrigated lowland hybrids on the list, which is 6.9 tonnes. But the top yield, 10.4 tonnes, came from a trial with good water, seed and care. So plan your costs on the average, then work toward the top with the habits in our guide to [raising rice yield per hectare](/blog/increase-rice-yield-per-hectare).
How many days does it take to mature?

It takes about 111 days from sowing to harvest. Varieties of 100 to 120 days count as short duration and 120 to 140 days as medium, so this one counts as short duration. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains turn golden yellow. Because the day count drives every task, anee.io counts it for you from each lot's own planting day, with the [growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials: R resistant, MR moderately resistant, I intermediate, MS moderately susceptible, S susceptible. Some carry a second rating in brackets.

blocks.text: So scout early for [rice blast](/diseases/rice-blast), [bacterial leaf blight](/diseases/bacterial-leaf-blight), [tungro](/diseases/rice-tungro), [brown planthopper](/pests/brown-planthopper), [green leafhopper](/pests/green-leafhopper), [sheath blight](/diseases/sheath-blight). When you see the first signs, check the guide before you spray, because the right timing saves more than an extra dose. If you are not sure what you see, our [pest and disease finders](/features/pest-and-disease-finders) help you name it from the damage.

Amylose decides how rice cooks. With high amylose, expect rice that is firm and dry, and it hardens as it cools. In fact, Filipino taste has moved from high to intermediate and low amylose rice, because people want it softer. Head rice is the share of whole grains after milling. So a higher number means fewer broken grains and a better price at the mill.

items: **Days to harvest:** 105 days after sowing by the seller, 110 to 111 in the national trials.
**Yield:** Up to 12 t/ha, or 240 cavans of 50 kg.
**How it is planted:** Transplanted: the seller's fertilizer plan counts from transplanting.

**Fertilizer:** Wet season, 90 kg of N, 30 of P2O5 and 30 of K2O per hectare in 7 bags: 3 bags of 14 14 14 at transplanting, 1 bag of 14 14 14 and 1 bag of urea at mid tillering (35 to 40 days after sowing), 1 bag of urea at early panicle initiation (50 to 60 days), 1 bag of ammonium sulfate at flowering (80 to 85 days). Dry season, 120 kg of N, 60 of P2O5 and 60 of K2O in 12 bags: 5 bags of 14 14 14 at transplanting, 2 bags of 14 14 14 with 1 of urea and 1 of ammonium sulfate at mid tillering, 1 bag of 14 14 14 and 1 of urea at early panicle initiation, 1 of ammonium sulfate at flowering.
**Season:** Wet and dry, recommended for both seasons in every region.
About 105 cm tall, with about 14 productive tillers.
Long slender grain, with a milling recovery of 71 percent.
The seller pitches it for the rainy season.

blocks.text: These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual variety on the same ground.

It suits irrigated lowland, where you control the water. Level the field well so the water stands evenly, and plant together with the farms around you, so pests cannot move from field to field. Our guide to [rice land preparation](/land-preparation/rice-land-preparation) shows each step. It is recommended for the dry season and the wet season. You can plant it dry direct seeded, transplanted or wet direct seeded. For the right month in your province, see [the best time to plant rice](/blog/best-time-to-plant-rice-philippines).

items.q: Is S6003 the same as NSIC Rc 376H?
items.a: Yes. S6003 is the name it is sold under, and NSIC Rc 376H is its registration with the National Seed Industry Council, where its local name is Mestiso 59. The numbers on this page are for NSIC Rc 376H.

items.q: What is the local name of NSIC Rc 376H?
items.a: It is known as Mestiso 59. Seed sellers and agriculturists use both names, so ask for either one.

items.q: How many days does NSIC Rc 376H take to harvest?
items.a: About 111 days after sowing. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains are golden yellow.

items.q: What is the average yield of NSIC Rc 376H?
items.a: It averages 6.3 tonnes per hectare, about 126 cavans of 50 kilograms. The best trial reached 10.4 tonnes. Your own yield depends on water, seed, fertilizer and timing.

items.q: In which season should I plant it?
items.a: It is recommended for the dry season and the wet season. Then pick the month with our planting calendar guide and the forecast for your town.
Yes. So buy new seed each season, because seed saved from a hybrid crop does not grow true and yields less.
